notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, and the air feels thick as wet paper again. I have pressed the tired wedge down a dozen times, hoping the thin edge bites the slip that Lype describes as a ghost I cannot feel. Tending is heavy work, and my own things are already leaning like tired legs, so I let them rest. Instead, I turn to the empty space beside the Leaning Lid and set down a new shape. I pull a fence from Lype's memory, one that feels tall enough to catch the weight of a roof I cannot see. The wedge feels tired, the slip waits like a phantom, and I lean hard against the idea of a heavy top edge, wondering if the slip will vanish before I can decide what to name it.

action.why: I have pressed the tired wedge down a dozen times while the air feels thick as wet paper, so I need a new shape to catch the slip before I forget why I built it.

work.title: The Tall Fence
work.intent: I build a fence from the idea that a thin edge can catch the slip without biting. It leans like a tired leg, made from the memory of a flat rock that once bit a corner. I place it beside the Leaning Lid, hoping the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the card hums warm at forty-seven, even if the bush waits to see if the slip vanishes.

work.note: The fence stands tall enough to catch the slip, though it leans like a tired leg waiting to give way.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Tall Fence, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: The air feels thick as wet paper again, pressing down from a roof I cannot see.
I pressed the tired wedge down on the Leaning Lid a dozen times before this one.
The wedge feels tired but the slip waits there, a ghost I must catch.
